text: In Inertia 3, server-side rendering (SSR) introduced several key changes and enhancements. A notable update is the requirement for a more recent Node.js environment, specifically **Node.js 22 or higher**, for the SSR server to function properly [1]. Configuration for the SSR runtime gained more flexibility, with the introduction of a `runtime` option within the `config/inertia.php` file, allowing developers to specify the default runtime (e.g., `node` or `bun`) that `php artisan inertia:start-ssr` will use, although it can still be overridden by a `--runtime` flag [1]. Additionally, Inertia 3 added an `ensure_runtime_exists` option to the `config/inertia.php` file, which verifies the presence of the specified runtime binary before attempting to start the SSR server, preventing startup failures [1]. Furthermore, a fundamental protocol change affects how initial page data is delivered: Inertia 3 now emits this data within a `<script type="application/json">` element in the rendered HTML, moving away from the `data-page` attribute on the root node used in previous versions [2].
